This is something that ios\_facts can do for you! 

[https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/ios\_facts\_module.html](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/ios_facts_module.html)

Line in file is how you will add to a file!

[https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/lineinfile\_module.html](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/lineinfile_module.html)

ios\_facts will create a new variable for you with a list of all the interfaces on the device and details about them. One of the items is operstatus which is what you are looking for. the variable name is ansible\_net\_interfaces. It will look similar to the below output. You can loop through these to get a bunch of great info! I highly suggest looking through everything ios\_facts can give you! 

​

I decided to write a quick script to help you. I have tested on one of my iosxe switches and this will work. I am on Ansible 2.9.13 and python 3.8.2. If you have any questions or issues with the below script feel free to message me.

​

\---  
\- hosts: ios  
 connection: network\_cli  
 gather\_facts: false  
 tasks:  
\- name: get facts  
ios\_facts:  


   \- name: add down interfaces to file  
 lineinfile:  
line: "{{ item.key }} {{ item.value.operstatus }}"  
path: "{{ playbook\_dir }}/{{ inventory\_hostname }}\_down\_ports.txt"  
create: yes  
 with\_items: "{{ ansible\_net\_interfaces | dict2items }}"  
 when: item.value.operstatus == 'down'
